## History
### Most Intriguing People of the Year
At the end of each year _People_ magazine famously selects 25 news-making individuals or couples who have received much media attention over the past 12 months and showcases them in a special year-end issue, the '25 Most Intriguing People of the Year'. This series of full-page features and half-page featurettes includes world leaders and political activists, famous actors and entertainers, elite athletes, prominent business people, accomplished scientists and occasionally members of the public whose stories have made an unusual impact in news or tabloid media.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-66)

## History
### 100 Most Beautiful People
_People_'s 100 Most Beautiful People is an annual list of 100 people judged to be the most beautiful individuals in the world. Until 2006, it was the 50 Most Beautiful People.
Julia Roberts holds the record for most times named, with five.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-67)Michelle Pfeiffer, Jennifer Aniston, and Kate Hudson have appeared twice.
In 2020, Goldie Hawn, Kate Hudson, and Hudson's daughter Rani became the first multigenerational cover stars of the Beautiful Issue. In addition, Hawn and her granddaughter concurrently became the oldest and youngest to cover the Beautiful Issue.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-68)

## History
### People Magazine Yearbook
People Magazine Yearbook is an annual publication released by publishers of _People_ magazine, currently Meredith Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-adweek-3) The Yearbook broadly covers all the major events that happened in the year that it covers. This includes socially relevant news events that made headlines around the world in general but more specifically in the United States. Besides the news headlines, it covers celebrity weddings, splits/divorces, births and deaths, and also scandalous events that generated much news when they happened. Over the years, it has covered headlining events in the world of Music (Grammy Awards), Movies (Oscar Awards, The Golden Globe Awards), and Television (Emmy Awards) in a bite sized recap of the event and the award winners. The People Yearbook has had the year (say, 2010) written in Bold accompanying the word "Yearbook" on the front cover since the People Yearbook 1995,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:1-69) although this gradually changed in the more recent editions. Since 2015, the "year" appeared in a more inconspicuous way on the front cover until the 2019 issue[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:0-70) and the bold style of writing the "year" made a comeback in the 2020 issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:4-71) The year also appears on the spine.

_People_'s 100 Most Beautiful People is an annual list of 100 people judged to be the most beautiful individuals in the world. Until 2006, it was the 50 Most Beautiful People.

## History
### People Magazine Yearbook
People Magazine Yearbook is an annual publication released by publishers of _People_ magazine, currently Meredith Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-adweek-3) The Yearbook broadly covers all the major events that happened in the year that it covers. This includes socially relevant news events that made headlines around the world in general but more specifically in the United States. Besides the news headlines, it covers celebrity weddings, splits/divorces, births and deaths, and also scandalous events that generated much news when they happened. Over the years, it has covered headlining events in the world of Music (Grammy Awards), Movies (Oscar Awards, The Golden Globe Awards), and Television (Emmy Awards) in a bite sized recap of the event and the award winners. The People Yearbook has had the year (say, 2010) written in Bold accompanying the word "Yearbook" on the front cover since the People Yearbook 1995,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:1-69) although this gradually changed in the more recent editions. Since 2015, the "year" appeared in a more inconspicuous way on the front cover until the 2019 issue[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:0-70) and the bold style of writing the "year" made a comeback in the 2020 issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:4-71) The year also appears on the spine.

In April 2012, Rihanna was included on TIME magazine’s annual TIME 100 list of the world’s most influential people. At only 24 years old, she was recognized in the list’s entertainment category during a period when her music career was rapidly expanding internationally. TIME published a tribute to Rihanna written by fashion designer Stella McCartney, who described her as a major young artist and highlighted her work with fans, friends and her foundation. Rihanna attended the TIME 100 Gala on April 24, 2012, at Frederick P. Rose Hall at Lincoln Center in New York City, where she also performed. The event brought together people from entertainment, business, politics and other fields represented on that year’s list. #### **About**
🕙**This webinar will take place 10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. Eastern Time.**
AACSB is organizing a **free webinar** featuring the editors of three practitioners’ journals: _California Management Review_, _Harvard Business Review_, and _Management and Business Review,_ inviting the deans, professors, alumni, and associated business community at all business schools, as well as its corporate members, to attend. The editors will discuss their review processes, subscription policies, and rules for classroom use of their articles.
After this presentation, a select group of deans and professors will be invited to ask questions.

#### **Meet the Speakers**
Amy Bernstein  Harvard Business Review
Amy Bernstein is Editor in Chief of Harvard Business Review, where she leads HBR’s editorial teams across the magazine, HBR.org, and HBR Press. She was previously the Editor of HBR’s magazine, which received two National Magazine Award nominations for general excellence during her tenure. Since 2020, she has also led the editorial strategy and content development for HBP’s Corporate Learning and Higher Education businesses. She was also cohost of HBR’s Women at Work podcast. Prior to joining HBR in 2011, Bernstein was Vice President, Global Thought Leadership at ManpowerGroup, and before that, she served as Executive Editor at strategy+business. She also held senior editorial positions at Business 2.0, The Industry Standard, Brill’s Content, and U.S. News & World Report.
Kora Gonzalez  Haas School of Business
Kora McClain-Gonzalez has spent 25 years at the University of California, Berkeley’s Haas School of Business, where she currently serves as Executive Editor of the California Management Review. In this role, she oversees the journal’s daily operations, leads content acquisition for its Spotlight section, and manages negotiations and partnerships involving new distribution channels. Prior to joining UC Berkeley, she taught writing and literature in the California State University system.
Christopher Ittner  Wharton School
Christopher Ittner is the EY Professor of Accounting at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. He received his Doctorate in Business Administration from Harvard University. Professor Ittner was previously Chair of Wharton’s Accounting Department and is Academic Director for Wharton’s online certificate programs in Business Analytics and Financial Planning & Analysis. His research focuses on the design, implementation, and performance consequences of performance measurement, cost management, and enterprise risk management systems. His articles have been published in leading academic accounting, economics, marketing, management, and operations management journals. He is co-editor-in-chief of Management and Business Research and has served as an editor for The Accounting Review, senior editor at Production and Operations Management, and associate editor for Accounting, Organizations and Society, Management Science, and several other academic journals. His research has received the American Accounting Association’s Notable Contribution to Management Accounting Literature and Impact on Management Accounting Practice awards.
Subodha Kumar  Temple University

#### **Meet the Speakers**
Subodha Kumar is the Paul R. Anderson Distinguished Chair Professor and the Founding Director of the Center for Business Analytics and Disruptive Technologies at Temple University. He also serves as the Concentration Director for the Ph.D. Program in Operations and Supply Chain Management. He serves on the boards of numerous organizations. He is the Co-Editor-in-Chief of Production and Operations Management (POM) and Management and Business Review (MBR). He is also the Executive Director of POM Society (POMS). Subodha has been named an INFORMS Information Systems Society Distinguished Fellow and a POMS Fellow. He has published more than 300 papers in reputed journals and refereed conference proceedings. He was ranked #1 worldwide for publishing in the UTD list of 24 leading journals and in Information Systems Research. He has also authored books, book chapters, Harvard Business School cases, and Ivey Business School cases. He is routinely cited in major media outlets.
Kalyan Singhal  Merrick School of Business
Kalyan Singhal is a Distinguished University Professor of Economics and Management at the Merrick School of Business, University of Baltimore. He founded the Production and Operations Management Society (POMS) in 1989 and its journal, Production and Operations Management, in 1992. He is the longest-serving editor of a top-ranked business journal on the BusinessWeek list of 20 and the Financial Times list of 50. Dr. Singhal is also the founder and co-editor-in-chief of the Management and Business Review (MBR). He is a Fellow of INFORMS and POMS.
David Vogel  Haas School of Business

#### **Meet the Speakers**
David Vogel is Professor Emeritus, the Haas School of Business and the Department of Political Science at the University of California, Berkeley. He joined the Berkeley faculty in 1974 . Vogel has written extensively on environmental policy at the state, national, and international levels. He is the author of nine books and several articles and essays on the national, comparative and international dimensions of consumer and environmental regulation. His most recent book is When Federal Climate Policy Works: Benefits, Business and Politics (with Roger Karapin) MIT Press, 2026. Vogel’s research has been recognized with lifetime achievement awards from the European Consortium for Political Research and the Section on Science, Technology and Environmental Politics of the American Political Science Association. He has edited the California Management Review since in 1982.

#### **Contact Us**
For more information, please contact**[events@aacsb.edu](mailto:events@aacsb.edu).**

## History
### People Magazine Yearbook
People Magazine Yearbook is an annual publication released by publishers of _People_ magazine, currently Meredith Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-adweek-3) The Yearbook broadly covers all the major events that happened in the year that it covers. This includes socially relevant news events that made headlines around the world in general but more specifically in the United States. Besides the news headlines, it covers celebrity weddings, splits/divorces, births and deaths, and also scandalous events that generated much news when they happened. Over the years, it has covered headlining events in the world of Music (Grammy Awards), Movies (Oscar Awards, The Golden Globe Awards), and Television (Emmy Awards) in a bite sized recap of the event and the award winners. The People Yearbook has had the year (say, 2010) written in Bold accompanying the word "Yearbook" on the front cover since the People Yearbook 1995,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:1-69) although this gradually changed in the more recent editions. Since 2015, the "year" appeared in a more inconspicuous way on the front cover until the 2019 issue[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:0-70) and the bold style of writing the "year" made a comeback in the 2020 issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:4-71) The year also appears on the spine.

# People Magazine Lists Most Intriguing of 2012
## INSIDE EDITION has the scoop on who made this year's People magazine list of the 25 Most Intriguing People.
A pregnant princess, a newly single lady, and a very sexy daddy-to-be. They all top _People_ magazine's list of the 25 Most Intriguing People of the year.
Katie Holmes makes the list for delivering the biggest suprise of the year, her divorce from Tom Cruise.
Michelle Tan, Senior Editor of _People_ told INSIDE EDITION, "We've seen a more independent, more confident Katie Holmes emerge."
Paula Deen is also on the list. In 2012, the queen of butter took heat after she revealed her Type 2 Diabetes diagnosis, but went on to drop 40 pounds.
Hunky Channing Tatum had a very big year. He broke through to major stardom in the stripper movie _Magic Mike_, was named _People_'s sexiest man alive, and he just found out he's going to be a dad.
Honey Boo Boo posed for the magazine, which hits newsstands Friday. Seven-year-old Alana Thompson, the year's most-talked-about reality star, is dressed up as Eloise at the Plaza.
"She's really just embracing her new stardom," said Tan.
And the No. 1 most intriguing person of 2012? It's Kate Middleton, who thrilled the world with the news of her pregnancy.
Tan said, "She's actually had a year of highs and lows. This summer she had the scandal with the topless photos in France. But her year capped off the year with amazing news that she's expecting."

_**People**_ is a popular American weekly magazine. It focuses on news about celebrities and interesting stories about everyday people. [Dotdash Meredith](https://kids.kiddle.co/People_Inc. "People Inc.") publishes the magazine. In 2009, _People_ was the most-read magazine in America. It had 46.6 million adult readers. By 2018, its readership changed to 35.9 million.
The magazine is well-known for its special yearly issues. These issues name the "World's Most Beautiful" people and the "Best & Worst Dressed" celebrities. _People'_ s main office is in New York City. It also has offices in Los Angeles and London.

## The History of People Magazine
The idea for _People_ magazine came from Andrew Heiskell. He was the chief executive of Time Inc. at the time. Richard Stolley was the first managing editor of _People_. He had worked for _Life_ magazine before.
Stolley wanted the magazine to focus on people. He said it was about "getting back to the people who are causing the news." This focus helped the magazine become successful very quickly. _People_ first came out on February 25, 1974.
The first issue was released for the week ending March 4, 1974. It had actress Mia Farrow on the cover. She was starring in the movie _The Great Gatsby_. The magazine was mostly black-and-white inside. It cost 35 cents when it first came out.
Many of the first team members came from _Life_ magazine. This included editors, writers, and photographers. They worked very hard to publish the magazine every week.

## The History of People Magazine
### People Magazine Around the World
In 1996, Time Inc. started a Spanish-language magazine. It was called _People en Español_. The idea came after a 1995 issue of _People_ sold out quickly. That issue had the singer Selena on the cover. Over time, _People en Español_ began to have its own original stories.
In 2002, _People_ launched _People Stylewatch_. This magazine focused on celebrity style, fashion, and beauty. It became very popular. In 2017, _People Stylewatch_ became digital-only.
In Australia, _People_ magazine is called _Who_. This is because another magazine already used the name _People_ there. An international version of _People_ has been published in Greece since 2010.

One reason for closing was less advertising. Also, there was more competition from other teen magazines and the internet. The website Teenpeople.com later joined People.com.

### Competition for Celebrity Photos
_People_ magazine is known for buying celebrity photos. Sometimes, they pay a lot of money for exclusive pictures. For example, _People_ reportedly paid $4.1 million for photos of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's newborn child, Shiloh. These photos set a record for their website. They got 26.5 million page views in one day.

At the end of each year, _People_ magazine picks 25 "Most Intriguing People of the Year." These are individuals or couples who have been in the news a lot. The list includes world leaders, actors, athletes, and scientists. Sometimes, it also features ordinary people with amazing stories.

## Army Veteran, TV Star & Now Vintage Oaks Property Owner
J.R. Martinez, the Army veteran who rose to the spotlight after winning Dancing With the Stars Season 13, plans to build his dream home in Vintage Oaks. Martinez recently purchased two homesites in one of the community’s gated neighborhoods and hopes to begin building soon.
Martinez was welcomed to Vintage Oaks by his new neighbors June 23 during a book signing event for his new book, “Full of Heart.” More than 150 neighbors and fans attended the event, which raised money for Operation FINALLY HOME, who has built two mortgage-free homes for wounded veterans in Vintage Oaks as well as over 40 more across the United States.

## Army Veteran, TV Star & Now Vintage Oaks Property Owner
##### About J.R.
In March of 2003, J.R. was deployed to Iraq, and on April 5, less than a month into his deployment, he was driving a Humvee in Karbala, when his left front tire hit a roadside bomb. The three other soldiers were ejected from the burning vehicle, but he was trapped inside and suffered smoke inhalation and severe burns to 34 percent of his body. J.R. claims that while he was fighting for his life and awaiting medical help his sister, Anabel, appeared to him giving him the strength to live.
J.R. was evacuated to a local medic station in Iraq and then to Landstuhl, Germany, for immediate care. He spent 34 months in recovery surgery at Brooke Army Medical Center (BAMC) in San Antonio, Texas, and underwent 33 different surgeries including skin grafts and cosmetic surgery. During recovery, a nurse asked him to speak to a burn patient, who had just seen his body for the first time and had become withdrawn. After a 45-minute visit, the patient opened the curtain letting light in his room and his heart. J.R. then understood the impact he had on this patient and decided to use his experience to help others. He continued to visit patients sharing his story and listening to theirs.

## Army Veteran, TV Star & Now Vintage Oaks Property Owner
##### The Past Two Years
The past two years have been quite something; not only did he and his dance partner, Karina Smirnoff, take ABC’s “Dancing With The Stars” season 13 coveted mirror ball trophy, he served as the 2012 Tournament of Roses Grand Marshal. J. R. was the cover of People Magazine, featured in their Sexiest Man Alive issue and one of the magazine’s 25 Most Intriguing People of 2011.Many awards and honors have been bestowed upon him including: Unsung Hero Award at the Lady in Red Gala; An Ivy Award for his work on behalf of the disabled in the entertainment community; recognized by the Los Angeles City Council for his dedication and passion to serving and inspiring those around him and the 2012 National Red Cross Spirit Award. ## The History of People Magazine
The idea for _People_ magazine came from Andrew Heiskell. He was the chief executive of Time Inc. at the time. Richard Stolley was the first managing editor of _People_. He had worked for _Life_ magazine before.
Stolley wanted the magazine to focus on people. He said it was about "getting back to the people who are causing the news." This focus helped the magazine become successful very quickly. _People_ first came out on February 25, 1974.
The first issue was released for the week ending March 4, 1974. It had actress Mia Farrow on the cover. She was starring in the movie _The Great Gatsby_. The magazine was mostly black-and-white inside. It cost 35 cents when it first came out.
Many of the first team members came from _Life_ magazine. This included editors, writers, and photographers. They worked very hard to publish the magazine every week.

People Magazine: Brand overview
Time Inc. launched People in 1974 after editor Andrew Heiskell noticed that Time stories about individual public figures regularly drew strong reader interest. He proposed a separate magazine focused on celebrities, personal stories, and public lives. The first issue appeared on March 4, 1974, with Mia Farrow from The Great Gatsby on the cover, and it sold out within days.
Under Richard Stolley, the magazine formed its early style through high-quality photography, short news items, interviews, and accessible reporting. The mix of celebrity coverage and human-interest stories helped People become one of the most-read magazines in the United States by the late 1970s.
In the 1980s, People expanded through annual special issues. “World’s Most Beautiful People,” later known as “Most Beautiful,” debuted in 1985 and became a regular format for the brand. In 1988, People en Español was launched to reach the growing Spanish-speaking audience in the United States.
The brand entered the digital era in 1996 with its website and later launched Teen People in 2000 for younger readers. In 2002, People introduced the “Sexiest Man Alive” issue, another annual feature tied to its image. People.com became a standalone entertainment news site in 2006, and in 2015 the company created People/Entertainment Weekly Network with Entertainment Weekly. Meredith bought Time Inc. for $2.8 billion in 2018; the service became PeopleTV in 2019, and by 2023 People remained a major American celebrity and entertainment media brand.
The publication’s emblem was created in 1974 for the first issue and has changed little since. The project’s ideational inspirers, Andrew Heskell and Richard Stolley, likely developed the sign’s concept. The compact inscription at the top of the cover indicated that the publication focuses on people: captivating destinies and personalities of interest to readers. The only significant change over time was the gradual move away from black lettering, which left a sad impression.

The magazine’s emblem is an inscription with a thin blue or pink outline. The transparent logo reflects the mission: to show popular and famous people from the inside. What are they interested in, passionate about, planning, and concerned about? Each issue is unique, and the letter colors reflect the cover stars’ personalities. The publication’s symbol can be called a chameleon because it changes color while keeping the main details.
> **What is People Magazine?**  
>   
>   
> A renowned American celebrity magazine is published weekly with a circulation of 3.5 million. It releases special compilations annually, selecting the most beautiful, interesting, and sexy people on the planet. The publication’s audience is about 36 million readers. They are owned by the IAC and held through the New York-based media company Dotdash Meredith.

### 1974 – 2002
The 1974 People magazine logo reflects when the publication first appeared on shelves. It looks simple and concise, but that is where its strength lies. The magazine’s title is set in a large, white, rounded-edged font. These forms symbolize accessibility and inclusiveness, as the magazine was aimed at a broad audience eager to learn about the lives of famous people and the interesting events they experienced.
The word “People” is printed in a bold, substantial font that immediately draws attention. This emphasizes the publication’s main focus: telling stories about people, their lives, and their challenges. The small “weekly” text is placed inside the last three letters, indicating the magazine’s weekly release. The smaller font for this word suggests that the main emphasis is on “People” as the publication’s core theme.
The logo’s black-and-white color scheme represents purity and neutrality, aligning with the magazine’s mission to present facts rather than impose opinions. The black background adds contrast, making the logo bold and noticeable. This minimalist design has remained recognizable for decades, maintaining its identity.

### 2002 – today
The modern version of the People logo appears bright and bold. The thick, rounded letters remain true to the original font, but now they have a thin, bright pink outline. This pink color symbolizes modernity and the desire to stay aligned with current trends.
The logo’s primary white background, framed by the pink outline, suggests something more significant beneath the surface. The magazine continues its tradition of showcasing celebrities’ external lives and delving into what happens behind the scenes of their glamorous careers and personal lives. The thin border around each letter creates a “mask” effect, hinting at people’s hidden emotions and experiences.
The logo’s style reflects the magazine’s essence: bright and contemporary, while deeply exploring its subjects’ personal stories. The dynamic design, with its play of colors and contrasts, emphasizes this. The pink accent conveys warmth and friendliness, attracting a younger, more female audience.
This emblem symbolizes the magazine’s transition from a traditional print publication to a more digital format. Always in tune with change, the magazine has transformed, maintaining its uniqueness while adapting to modern challenges such as social media and mobile platforms.

People Magazine: Brand overview
Time Inc. launched People in 1974 after editor Andrew Heiskell noticed that Time stories about individual public figures regularly drew strong reader interest. He proposed a separate magazine focused on celebrities, personal stories, and public lives. The first issue appeared on March 4, 1974, with Mia Farrow from The Great Gatsby on the cover, and it sold out within days.
Under Richard Stolley, the magazine formed its early style through high-quality photography, short news items, interviews, and accessible reporting. The mix of celebrity coverage and human-interest stories helped People become one of the most-read magazines in the United States by the late 1970s.
In the 1980s, People expanded through annual special issues. “World’s Most Beautiful People,” later known as “Most Beautiful,” debuted in 1985 and became a regular format for the brand. In 1988, People en Español was launched to reach the growing Spanish-speaking audience in the United States.
The brand entered the digital era in 1996 with its website and later launched Teen People in 2000 for younger readers. In 2002, People introduced the “Sexiest Man Alive” issue, another annual feature tied to its image. People.com became a standalone entertainment news site in 2006, and in 2015 the company created People/Entertainment Weekly Network with Entertainment Weekly. Meredith bought Time Inc. for $2.8 billion in 2018; the service became PeopleTV in 2019, and by 2023 People remained a major American celebrity and entertainment media brand.
The publication’s emblem was created in 1974 for the first issue and has changed little since. In 1973, Vogue became a monthly publication.[29] Under editor-in-chief Grace Mirabella, the magazine underwent extensive editorial and stylistic changes in response to changes of its target audience.[30] Mirabella states that she was chosen in an effort to change Vogue, because "women weren't interested in reading about or buying clothes that served no purpose in their changing lives."[31] She was selected to make the magazine appeal to "the free, working, "liberated" woman of the seventies.[31] The magazine also took a different approach in terms of interviews, arts coverage, and articles. Later this stylistic change fell out of favor in the 1980s, Mirabella was fired.[31]

1988–2025: Anna Wintour leadershipedit  
See also: Anna Wintour § Condé Nast

In July 1988, with Vogue losing readership and advertising to its rival Elle, Anna Wintour was named editor-in-chief.[32][33] Noted for her trademark bob cut and sunglasses, Wintour attempted to revitalize the brand by making it feel younger and more approachable;[34] she directed the focus towards new and accessible concepts of "fashion" for a wider audience.[35] Wintour's influence allowed the magazine to maintain its high circulation with staff introducing new trends that a broader audience could conceivably afford.[35]
Throughout her reign at Vogue, Wintour accomplished her goals to revitalize the magazine and oversaw production of some of its largest editions in terms of length. The September 2012 edition measured 916 pages, which was the highest ever for a monthly magazine.[33]
The contrast of Wintour's vision with that of her predecessors was noted as striking by observers, both critics and defenders. Amanda Fortini, fashion and style contributor for Slate, argues that her policy has been beneficial for Vogue, delivering it from what some critics had termed its boring "beige years".[36] {{blockquote| Among Condé Nast executives there was worry that the grand dame of fashion publications was losing ground to Elle, which in just three years had reached a paid circulation of 851,000, compared to Vogue's 1.2 million. Thus, Condé Nast publisher Si Newhouse brought in the 38-year-old Wintour, who, through the editor-in-chief positions at British Vogue and House & Garden had become known not only for her cutting-edge visual sense, but also for her ability to radically revamp a magazine—to shake things up. Healthy body initiativeedit
May 2013 marked the first anniversary of a healthy body initiative that was signed by the magazine's international editors—the initiative represents a commitment from the editors to promote positive body images within the content of Vogue's numerous editions. Vogue Australia editor Edwina McCann explained:
In the magazine we're moving away from those very young, very thin girls. A year down the track, we ask ourselves what can Vogue do about it? And an issue like this [June 2013 issue] is what we can do about it. If I was aware of a girl being ill on a photo shoot I wouldn't allow that shoot to go ahead, or if a girl had an eating disorder I would not shoot her.[70]

In 2009, the feature-length documentary The September Issue was released; it was an inside view of the production of the record-breaking September 2007 issue of U.S. Vogue, directed by R. J. Cutler. The film was shot over eight months as Wintour prepared the issue, and included testy exchanges between Wintour and her creative director Grace Coddington. The issue became the largest ever published at the time; over 5 pounds in weight and 840 pages in length, a world record for a monthly magazine.[110] That record has been broken by Vogue's September 2012 issue, which came in at 916 pages.[111]
Also in 2012, HBO released a documentary entitled In Vogue: The Editor's Eye, in conjunction with the 120th anniversary of the magazine. Drawing on Vogue's extensive archives, the film featured behind-the-scenes interviews with longtime Vogue editors, including Wintour, Coddington, Tonne Goodman, Babs Simpson, Hamish Bowles, and Phyllis Posnick.[112] Celebrated subjects and designers in the fashion industry, such as Nicole Kidman, Sarah Jessica Parker, Linda Evangelista, Vera Wang, and Marc Jacobs, also appear in the film. The editors share personal stories about collaborating with top photographers, such as Leibovitz, and the various day-to-day responsibilities and interactions of a fashion editor at Vogue. The film was directed and produced by Fenton Bailey and Randy Barbato. In October 2012, Vogue also released a book titled Vogue: The Editor's Eye to complement the documentary.[113]

In July 1988, with Vogue losing readership and advertising to its rival Elle, Anna Wintour was named editor-in-chief.[32][33] Noted for her trademark bob cut and sunglasses, Wintour attempted to revitalize the brand by making it feel younger and more approachable;[34] she directed the focus towards new and accessible concepts of "fashion" for a wider audience.[35] Wintour's influence allowed the magazine to maintain its high circulation with staff introducing new trends that a broader audience could conceivably afford.[35]
Throughout her reign at Vogue, Wintour accomplished her goals to revitalize the magazine and oversaw production of some of its largest editions in terms of length. The September 2012 edition measured 916 pages, which was the highest ever for a monthly magazine.[33]
The contrast of Wintour's vision with that of her predecessors was noted as striking by observers, both critics and defenders. Amanda Fortini, fashion and style contributor for Slate, argues that her policy has been beneficial for Vogue, delivering it from what some critics had termed its boring "beige years".[36] {{blockquote| Among Condé Nast executives there was worry that the grand dame of fashion publications was losing ground to Elle, which in just three years had reached a paid circulation of 851,000, compared to Vogue's 1.2 million. Thus, Condé Nast publisher Si Newhouse brought in the 38-year-old Wintour, who, through the editor-in-chief positions at British Vogue and House & Garden had become known not only for her cutting-edge visual sense, but also for her ability to radically revamp a magazine—to shake things up. Although she has had a strong impact on the magazine, Wintour has been pinned as being cold and difficult to work with.[33]

Launched in 2011 by Condé Nast Digital, Voguepedia is a fashion encyclopedia that also includes an archive of every issue of Vogue's American edition since 1892.[119] Only Vogue staff are permitted to contribute to the encyclopedia, unlike the VogueEncyclo—hosted by Vogue Italia—that receives contributions from anyone.[120] As of May 9, 2013, the site was not fully functional; code still showed in search results and only certain search terms yielded results.[121]
Websiteedit
Vogue has also created an easily navigable website that includes six different content categories for viewers to explore. The website includes an archive with issues from 1892 forward for those whom subscribe for the website. The magazines online are the same as those that were printed in that time and are not cut or shortened from the original content.[122]

The app was introduced on April 26, 2016, as a way for the magazine to become more mobile friendly. The Vogue app displays content on mobile devices and gives people the ability to view the magazine content wherever they go. The app has new content every day and people can choose to receive content recommended just for their taste. In addition, the app allows one to save stories for later and or read offline. Vogue Businessedit
The online fashion industry publication was launched in January 2019. The new property aims at offering a global perspective on the fashion industry with industry insights. Although sharing the Vogue brand name, Vogue Business is operated as a separate business entity with an independent editorial team. In June 2019, Vogue Business launched the Vogue Business Talent, a platform that promotes vacancies from international fashion brands and companies with the goal to match professionals with their job opportunities.[125][126]

### People Magazine Yearbook
People Magazine Yearbook is an annual publication released by publishers of _People_ magazine, currently Meredith Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-adweek-3) The Yearbook broadly covers all the major events that happened in the year that it covers. This includes socially relevant news events that made headlines around the world in general but more specifically in the United States. Besides the news headlines, it covers celebrity weddings, splits/divorces, births and deaths, and also scandalous events that generated much news when they happened. Over the years, it has covered headlining events in the world of Music (Grammy Awards), Movies (Oscar Awards, The Golden Globe Awards), and Television (Emmy Awards) in a bite sized recap of the event and the award winners. The People Yearbook has had the year (say, 2010) written in Bold accompanying the word "Yearbook" on the front cover since the People Yearbook 1995,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:1-69) although this gradually changed in the more recent editions. Since 2015, the "year" appeared in a more inconspicuous way on the front cover until the 2019 issue[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:0-70) and the bold style of writing the "year" made a comeback in the 2020 issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:4-71) The year also appears on the spine.

The annual feature the "Sexiest Man Alive" is billed as a benchmark of male attractiveness and typically includes only famous people and celebrities. _**People**_ is a popular American weekly magazine. It focuses on news about celebrities and interesting stories about everyday people. [Dotdash Meredith](https://kids.kiddle.co/People_Inc. "People Inc.") publishes the magazine. In 2009, _People_ was the most-read magazine in America. It had 46.6 million adult readers. By 2018, its readership changed to 35.9 million.
The magazine is well-known for its special yearly issues. These issues name the "World's Most Beautiful" people and the "Best & Worst Dressed" celebrities. _People'_ s main office is in New York City. It also has offices in Los Angeles and London.

## The History of People Magazine
The idea for _People_ magazine came from Andrew Heiskell. He was the chief executive of Time Inc. at the time. Richard Stolley was the first managing editor of _People_. He had worked for _Life_ magazine before.
Stolley wanted the magazine to focus on people. He said it was about "getting back to the people who are causing the news." This focus helped the magazine become successful very quickly. _People_ first came out on February 25, 1974.
The first issue was released for the week ending March 4, 1974. It had actress Mia Farrow on the cover. She was starring in the movie _The Great Gatsby_. The magazine was mostly black-and-white inside. It cost 35 cents when it first came out.
Many of the first team members came from _Life_ magazine. This included editors, writers, and photographers. They worked very hard to publish the magazine every week.

## The History of People Magazine
### People Magazine Around the World
In 1996, Time Inc. started a Spanish-language magazine. It was called _People en Español_. The idea came after a 1995 issue of _People_ sold out quickly. That issue had the singer Selena on the cover. Over time, _People en Español_ began to have its own original stories.
In 2002, _People_ launched _People Stylewatch_. This magazine focused on celebrity style, fashion, and beauty. It became very popular. In 2017, _People Stylewatch_ became digital-only.
In Australia, _People_ magazine is called _Who_. This is because another magazine already used the name _People_ there. An international version of _People_ has been published in Greece since 2010.

_People_ magazine is known for buying celebrity photos. Sometimes, they pay a lot of money for exclusive pictures. For example, _People_ reportedly paid $4.1 million for photos of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's newborn child, Shiloh. These photos set a record for their website. ## History
### People Magazine Yearbook
People Magazine Yearbook is an annual publication released by publishers of _People_ magazine, currently Meredith Corporation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-adweek-3) The Yearbook broadly covers all the major events that happened in the year that it covers. This includes socially relevant news events that made headlines around the world in general but more specifically in the United States. Besides the news headlines, it covers celebrity weddings, splits/divorces, births and deaths, and also scandalous events that generated much news when they happened. Over the years, it has covered headlining events in the world of Music (Grammy Awards), Movies (Oscar Awards, The Golden Globe Awards), and Television (Emmy Awards) in a bite sized recap of the event and the award winners. The People Yearbook has had the year (say, 2010) written in Bold accompanying the word "Yearbook" on the front cover since the People Yearbook 1995,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:1-69) although this gradually changed in the more recent editions. Since 2015, the "year" appeared in a more inconspicuous way on the front cover until the 2019 issue[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:0-70) and the bold style of writing the "year" made a comeback in the 2020 issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-:4-71) The year also appears on the spine.

## The History of People Magazine
The idea for _People_ magazine came from Andrew Heiskell. He was the chief executive of Time Inc. at the time. Richard Stolley was the first managing editor of _People_. He had worked for _Life_ magazine before.
Stolley wanted the magazine to focus on people. He said it was about "getting back to the people who are causing the news." This focus helped the magazine become successful very quickly. _People_ first came out on February 25, 1974.
The first issue was released for the week ending March 4, 1974. It had actress Mia Farrow on the cover. She was starring in the movie _The Great Gatsby_. The magazine was mostly black-and-white inside. It cost 35 cents when it first came out.
Many of the first team members came from _Life_ magazine. This included editors, writers, and photographers. They worked very hard to publish the magazine every week.

## The History of People Magazine
### People Magazine Around the World
In 1996, Time Inc. started a Spanish-language magazine. It was called _People en Español_. The idea came after a 1995 issue of _People_ sold out quickly. That issue had the singer Selena on the cover. Over time, _People en Español_ began to have its own original stories.
In 2002, _People_ launched _People Stylewatch_. This magazine focused on celebrity style, fashion, and beauty. It became very popular. In 2017, _People Stylewatch_ became digital-only.
In Australia, _People_ magazine is called _Who_. This is because another magazine already used the name _People_ there. An international version of _People_ has been published in Greece since 2010.

## History[]
### Sexiest Man Alive[]
The annual feature the "Sexiest Man Alive" is billed as a benchmark of male attractiveness and typically includes only famous people and celebrities. It is determined using a procedure similar to the procedure used for _Time_'s Person of the Year. The origin of the title was a discussion on a planned story on Mel Gibson. Someone exclaimed, "Oh my God, he is the sexiest man alive!" And someone else said, "You should use that as a cover line."[[21]](https://culture.fandom.com/wiki/People_(magazine)#cite_note-21)
For the first decade or so, the feature appeared at uneven intervals. Originally awarded in the wintertime, it shifted around the calendar, resulting in gaps as short as seven months and as long as a year and a half (with no selection at all during 1994, however 21 years later People selected Keanu Reeves to fill the 1994 gap, the runners up for that year includes Hugh Grant and Jim Carrey). Since 1997, the dates have settled between mid-November and early December.
Dates of magazine issues, winners, ages of winners at the time of selection, and pertinent comments are listed below.
As of 2016, John F. Kennedy, Jr. and Patrick Swayze are the only winners to have died since winning. Kennedy, Adam Levine and David Beckham are the only non-actors to have won the award.
